doc.title: Updating Another Repository
doc.paragraph: If you have your own package, extension or command that was built against an older Adaptive Framework, a good deal of the C API has changed under it. This chapter walks through bringing it up to date, in the order we have found works best. Each step is something you can search your sources for, fix, and build before going on to the next. whats-new.md, at the root of the afw repository, has the full list of changes, in its C programmers section.

steps.step: Rebuild and reinstall against the Adaptive Framework you have installed now. Extensions and commands built against an older libafw are not supported with a newer one, even when they still load.

Remove APR. Adaptive Framework no longer uses it, so your CMake and pkg-config files do not need apr-1 or apr-util because of it, and afw_common.h no longer includes apr_strings.h. Search for apr_, APR_ and get_apr_pool, and use the replacements in the table below.
Include only afw.h. Package *_declare_helpers.h headers are no longer generated; AFW_DECLARE and AFW_DEFINE come from afw_common.h.

Pass a pool everywhere memory is allocated. The afw_xctx_malloc, calloc and free macros are gone: use afw_pool_malloc(), afw_pool_calloc() and afw_pool_free_memory() with the dest p. afw_pool_create() now makes a heap like its parent; a tracker is afw_pool_tracker_create(). afw_pool_destroy() no longer runs cleanup functions, so call afw_pool_run_cleanups() first if you need them, or just use afw_pool_release().
Pass property names as values. Object get, set, has and remove take a const afw_value_t * property name, so afw_s_foo becomes afw_v_foo, or your own package's *_v_foo.

Fix the format strings. In afw_utf8_printf() and AFW_THROW_ERROR_FZ(), replace AFW_UTF8_FMT with %ku and pass the const afw_utf8_t * itself instead of AFW_UTF8_FMT_ARG(s). Leave AFW_UTF8_FMT alone in fprintf() and other C library calls. Use %ks for C strings that might not be valid UTF-8. See Programming in C.

Check the typed getters. A name with _as_ and a data type, such as afw_object_get_property_as_string(), now returns the typed value; the C value inside it is the _internal form. Getters no longer take a dest p, and afw_array_push_internal() and its relatives are gone (use afw_array_push_value()).

Check what you create, keep and release, using the rules in Programming in C. Objects and arrays that used to be made with create_managed because they owned a pool are now create_unmanaged_new_p; create_managed now means fully managed, and its caller releases it.

row.column: afw_utf8_create (the old one, which pointed when it could)
afw_thread_mutex_create(flags, p, xctx) and afw_thread_rwlock_*; native threads are afw_os_thread_*
afw_value_create_pooled_copy, afw_object_create_pooled_copy. afw_value_clone now makes an independent copy a script may change, which you release.
